findings.title: Exhaustiveness guard uses a module-level `assert`
findings.description: `_BUCKET_ROWS` is checked against `set(TickSessionStatus)` with a bare `assert` at import time. Under `python -O` the check is stripped. A new status enum member would then drop out of the report with no error. That breaks the project rule against silent fallbacks. Raise an explicit error instead, or assert exhaustiveness in a unit test. A `_label`/`match` over the enum would also work.

findings.title: Status, condition and check values are bare strings rather than enums
findings.description: `CoverageSession.condition`, `.status` and `.check` are `str`. `MISMATCH, OK = "mismatch", "ok"` are module constants rather than a `StrEnum`. `ProductStatus.buckets` is keyed by `str`, and the renderer indexes it with `s.value`. The Python rules and the project's "define it once" rule call for `StrEnum`. The values also feed the `--json` contract that slice 230 will reuse. The tests compare the literals `"ok"` and `"complete"`, which scatters the comparison values.

findings.title: `Any`-typed connection in the CLI read helpers weakens strict pyright
findings.description: `_read` takes `Callable[[Any, str], ...]`, and the nested `read(conn: Any, ...)` in `tick_coverage` is `Any` too. The repo already has a `Conn` alias in `manifest_reads`. The `Any` hides a type mismatch from strict pyright. Type both with `Conn`.

findings.title: Spread filtering relies on dataclass equality and O(n·m) membership
findings.description: `[c for c in lines if c not in spreads]` filters by full `ContractLine` equality against a list. It is quadratic, and it expresses "not a spread" indirectly. Filter on `c.instrument_class != SPREAD_CLASS` instead, which also removes the intermediate list for the non-spread case. `_product_status` is also close to the ~50-line guideline and mixes scope resolution, bucket counting and DTO assembly. Splitting the DTO assembly out would help.

findings.title: Raw-count session assignment can double-count at touching session boundaries
findings.description: The join uses `t.ts_event BETWEEN s.open_ns AND s.close_ns`, which is inclusive on both ends. A trade stamped exactly at a shared boundary would count in two sessions if the calendar ever produced touching sessions. The CME calendar leaves a gap, so this is latent. A half-open interval would make the intent explicit and match `days_touched`'s closed-interval handling.

findings.title: Render helpers have no direct unit tests
findings.description: `age()` and the line builders are only covered through the integration CLI tests. A small parametrized unit test of `age` (minutes, hours, days) and of the "never observed" and "no tier" branches would be cheap. Coverage of the build and read layers, the exit codes (1, 3, 4) and the `--json` shape is good.

findings.title: Positive observations
findings.description:
- The `except Exception` in `run_mapped` is a documented process-boundary handler that re-raises unmapped errors.
- `TickDatabaseUnreachable` subclasses `TickPreflightError`, so the writers' behaviour is unchanged while the read verbs map it to the storage exit.
- Blocking calendar access runs through `asyncio.to_thread`, so it does not stall the event loop.
- The calendar helper refactor into `utc_midnight` and `days_touched` removes duplicated logic.
- Test fixtures delete rows only from throwaway databases and by primary key, which meets the database-safety rules.

structured_findings.summary: Status, condition and check values are bare strings rather than enums
`Any`-typed connection in the CLI read helpers weakens strict pyright
Spread filtering relies on dataclass equality and O(n·m) membership
Raw-count session assignment can double-count at touching session boundaries
Render helpers have no direct unit tests
